title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $F:V(G)\xrightarrow{}2^{\mathbb{N}}$. If $|F(v)|<\frac{1}{2}\deg(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$, then $G$ has an $F$-avoiding orientation.
context_text: Akbari, Dalirrooyfard, Ehsani, Ozeki, and Sherkati introduced this conjecture in the study of orientations avoiding forbidden out-degree lists. They established the statement when $\frac{1}{2}$ is replaced by $\frac{1}{4}$. The sharpness of the $\frac{1}{2}$ bound is witnessed by $K_{2k+1}$ with $F(v)=\{k,k+1,\dots,2k-1\}$.
attributed_to: Akbari, Dalirrooyfard, Ehsani, Ozeki, and Sherkati
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture under the stronger bound $|F(v)|<\lfloor\frac{1}{3}\deg(v)\rfloor$ for all graphs, and further improves the coefficient to $\sqrt{2}-1-o(1)\approx 0.414$ when the maximum degree is subexponential in terms of the minimum degree.
notes: The condition $|F(v)|<\frac{1}{2}\deg(v)$ was truncated in the extracted theorem environment; it is completed here from the abstract and surrounding context.

title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $F:V(G)\xrightarrow{}2^{\mathbb{N}}$. If $G$ has an orientation $D$ such that $|F(v)|\leq\deg_{D}^{+}(v)$ for every $v\in V(G)$, then $G$ has an $F$-avoiding orientation.
context_text: This companion conjecture from Akbari et al. relates the size of each forbidden list to the out-degree of the corresponding vertex in a fixed reference orientation rather than to its total degree. It is motivated by the fact that every graph admits an orientation with $\deg_D^+(v)\geq\lfloor\deg_G(v)/2\rfloor$, which would make Conjecture 1.2 a strengthening of Conjecture 1.1.
attributed_to: Akbari, Dalirrooyfard, Ehsani, Ozeki, and Sherkati
paper_contribution: The paper's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz-based sufficient condition (Theorem 1.6) applies to both conjectures and yields new partial results toward each.
notes: The condition in the extracted theorem environment was truncated; the quantitative hypothesis is reconstructed from the surrounding context describing the motivation for Conjecture 1.2.

title: Question 6.1
statement_text: Does every graph $G$ have a spanning subgraph with an Alon-Tarsi orientation in which each vertex $v$ has out-degree at least $\frac{1}{2}(\deg_{G}(v)-1)$?
context_text: For an orientation $D$ of a graph $G$, a spanning subgraph of $G$ is Eulerian (with respect to $D$) if every vertex has equal in- and out-degree in it; $EE(D)$ and $EO(D)$ count the Eulerian subgraphs with an even, resp. odd, number of edges, and $D$ is an Alon-Tarsi orientation if $EE(D)\neq EO(D)$. The Alon-Tarsi number $\operatorname{AT}(G)$ is the minimum $k$ such that $G$ has an Alon-Tarsi orientation of maximum out-degree less than $k$; Alon and Tarsi proved that the list chromatic number satisfies $\mathrm{ch}(G)\le\operatorname{AT}(G)$. Given $F:V(G)\to2^{\mathbb{N}}$, an orientation $D$ of $G$ is $F$-avoiding if $\deg^+_D(v)\notin F(v)$ for every vertex $v$. Akbari et al. conjectured that $G$ has an $F$-avoiding orientation whenever $|F(v)|\le\frac12(\deg_G(v)-1)$ for every $v$ (sharp, e.g. for $K_{2k+1}$), and proved that if some spanning subgraph $H$ of $G$ has an Alon-Tarsi orientation $D$ with $|F(v)|\le\deg^+_D(v)$ for every $v$, then $G$ has an $F$-avoiding orientation. A positive answer would therefore prove that conjecture for every graph, in a stronger form (combined with a result of Huang, Wong and Zhu on $\operatorname{AT}(K_n-N)$ for a maximum matching $N$, this approach already proves the conjecture for complete graphs). The authors prove the conjecture with coefficient roughly $\frac13$ instead of $\frac12$ (and $\sqrt2-1$ when the maximum degree is $e^{o(\delta)}$). An affirmative answer would also imply that every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$ has a subgraph $H$ with at least $|E(G)|-n/2$ edges satisfying $\operatorname{AT}(H)\le\lfloor\frac12\Delta+\frac32\rfloor$. If the answer is negative, one can still ask the same question with $-1$ replaced by an arbitrary constant $-C$.

title: Question 6.2
statement_text: Does there exist a constant $C$ such that every graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a matching $M$ such that $\operatorname{AT}(G-M)\leq\frac{1}{2}\Delta+C$?
context_text: For an orientation $D$ of a graph $G$, a spanning subgraph of $G$ is Eulerian (with respect to $D$) if every vertex has equal in- and out-degree in it; $EE(D)$ and $EO(D)$ count the Eulerian subgraphs with an even, resp. odd, number of edges, and $D$ is an Alon-Tarsi orientation if $EE(D)\neq EO(D)$. The Alon-Tarsi number $\operatorname{AT}(G)$ is the minimum $k$ such that $G$ has an Alon-Tarsi orientation of maximum out-degree less than $k$; Alon and Tarsi proved that the list chromatic number satisfies $\mathrm{ch}(G)\le\operatorname{AT}(G)$. The question is motivated by the authors' question whether every graph has a spanning subgraph with an Alon-Tarsi orientation in which every vertex $v$ has out-degree at least $\frac12(\deg_G(v)-1)$ (related to $F$-avoiding orientations), a positive answer to which would give a subgraph $H$ with at least $|E(G)|-n/2$ edges and $\operatorname{AT}(H)\le\lfloor\frac12\Delta+\frac32\rfloor$. The requirement that $M$ be a matching is inspired by two results showing that removing a matching can lower a coloring bound: Zhu proved that planar graphs have Alon-Tarsi number at most $5$ (tight), while Grytczuk and Zhu showed that every planar graph has a matching $M$ with $\operatorname{AT}(G-M)\le4$; and although $\chi(G)\le\Delta+1$ is tight for cliques, every graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a matching $M$ with $\chi(G-M)\le\lceil\frac{\Delta+1}{2}\rceil$. If the answer is affirmative one may ask for the optimal $C$; it cannot be smaller than $\frac12$, since for odd $n$ and any maximum matching $M$ of $K_n$, $\operatorname{AT}(K_n-M)=\frac{n+1}{2}$.
